mechanism_narrative: A rising GDPC1 indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in UNRATE suggests labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth may slow.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and PAYEMS increase, it indicates strong supply and labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both INDPRO and PAYEMS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in HOUST suggests strong housing demand, which could lead to positive S&P 500 returns as related sectors may perform well.
failure_condition: HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% may lead to inflation concerns, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% but S&P 500 returns are positive in the next 5 days more than 45% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases, it signals strong consumer demand and a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in PAYEMS during a late-cycle expansion may indicate peak employment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are positive over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.
